To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## Three framing points before the issues

1. **The "[STANDARD]" tags and the "Reviewer Efficiency Note" do not bind us.** They are the Seller's own labels. They ask us to skip scrutiny of the clauses that matter most: cap, thresholds, time limits, reliance, knowledge, Bluefen, Riverlark and Ironquay. I have reviewed every clause on its merits.
2. **The "settled at principal level / FINAL" claim is not supported.** Our playbook records no written authority from Amelia Frost for any fallback, including the 20% cap or 18-month period. Unless she confirms otherwise in writing, identifying this draft, nothing here is agreed.
3. **The "market context" preamble is advocacy, not evidence.** Our positions come from our playbook, not the Seller's description of market practice.

Helpfully, the Seller's own Disclosure Letter confirms several gaps. Bluefen consent is not delivered, Riverlark is not repaid, bonuses are not in the funds flow, and Ironquay has no payment receipt. These admissions support our positions.

---

## Issue-by-issue review

**SPA-N-001 General liability cap**
- **Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000 (cl. 12.1).
- **Buyer wants:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- **Recommendation: REJECT; counter at 25%.** The 20% fallback needs Amelia Frost's prior written authority for this draft, and none exists.

**SPA-N-002 De minimis and basket**
- **Seller:** AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 basket, excess only (cl. 12.2).
- **Buyer wants:** AUD 5,000 de minimis; AUD 50,000 basket, recoverable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- **Recommendation: REJECT.** The Seller's figures are 5x our thresholds, and an excess-only basket permanently strips the first AUD 250,000 of valid claims.

**SPA-N-003 General claims time limit**
- **Seller:** 18 months, plus a rule that "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (cl. 12.3/13).
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months for general claims, with separate periods for Fundamental, Tax and IP, and fraud excluded.
- **Recommendation: REJECT both.** 18 months is an unapproved fallback, and the default-to-all-claims rule is a hidden override of every other regime.

**SPA-N-004 Fundamental/Title regime**
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties share the general cap and time limits "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer wants:** A separate regime with a 100% cap, at least six years, and no general basket, de minimis or knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation: REJECT.** If title fails, the Buyer has bought nothing, so recovery capped at 20% of price is no protection.

**SPA-N-005 Fraud carve-out**
- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl. 9.3/12.8/20.5). There is no fraud carve-out.
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- **Recommendation: REJECT; insert an express carve-out.** This is non-waivable under our playbook and cannot be traded.

**SPA-N-006 Disclosure scope**
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the whole data room, the Accounts, statutory registers and public records (DL 1.1–1.2).
- **Buyer wants:** Only specific, fair disclosure against identified warranties, with enough detail to assess nature and scope.
- **Recommendation: REJECT; delete DL 1.1–1.2.** Whole-data-room and public-register disclosure is expressly excluded by our playbook and would hollow out the warranties.

**SPA-N-007 Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter known to the Buyer or its advisers, or discoverable from the data room or public records (cl. 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** Delete the clause. Any knowledge qualifier must run to named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry, and must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation: REJECT; delete.** Read with the disclosure clause, it would extinguish claims for exactly the issues we found in due diligence and are indemnifying against.

**SPA-N-008 Bluefen consent**
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours; the condition is treated as satisfied on delivery of the written consent (cl. 3/6.3). DL 2 admits no consent and no evidence that the cl. 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- **Buyer wants:** An effective consent plus evidence that its conditions are satisfied, as a Condition Precedent before Completion.
- **Recommendation: REJECT.** Bluefen is about 30% of revenue (~AUD 3.6m), so reasonable endeavours and consent-on-delivery are insufficient.

**SPA-N-009 Riverlark facility**
- **Seller:** Release "to be provided following Completion" (cl. 2/7). DL 3 confirms no repayment and no discharge.
- **Buyer wants:** A current payout letter, direct repayment of about AUD 3.2m from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion.
- **Recommendation: REJECT.** A post-Completion release would need an irrevocable undertaking plus Amelia Frost approval, neither of which is offered.

**SPA-N-010 Employee bonuses**
- **Seller:** The AUD 420,000 DD-005 bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised in the funds flow. DL 5 is silent on on-costs.
- **Buyer wants:** The AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs (payroll tax, super) either as a specific funds-flow line item or as a Debt/price deduction, or seller-funded with an indemnity.
- **Recommendation: REJECT the silent exclusion.** Without a line item, the Company pays these after Completion and the Buyer bears the cost.

**SPA-N-011 Ironquay IP indemnity**
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the specific SOW3 payment and is "adequate" (cl. 11.1).
- **Buyer wants:** A broader indemnity covering title, transfer and infringement losses for the SOW3 Project Materials, preserving the SOW3 cure (payment plus confirmatory assignment). The AUD 180,000 should be treated as unverified, neither confirmed owed nor confirmed paid.
- **Recommendation: REJECT; broaden.** DL 4 confirms no payment receipt or assignment, so IP ownership itself is at risk, not only a fee.

**SPA-N-012 Export/privacy incident (DD-006)**
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material" (cl. 4.6/Sch 6).
- **Buyer wants:** Covenants to preserve logs, complete the investigation, and provide regular updates and access before Completion. We should not assume a confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or loss figure, and should not accept the Seller's assumption of immateriality either.
- **Recommendation: REJECT the materiality characterisation; add the covenants.** DL 6 itself says scope, access and notification status are unknown for about 1,240 records.

**SPA-N-013 Sandbar renewals**
- **Seller:** AUD 330,000 (3 × 110,000) of "ordinary-course operating costs."
- **Buyer wants:** An assessment of timing, scope, terminability and accrual, plus supporting information. This is not an automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Recommendation: HOLD and request information.** DL 8 does not say whether the renewals are ordinary-course, so neither side's label is established yet.

**SPA-N-014 Category separation**
- **Seller:** A single general regime governs all claims through the "all Claims" language in cl. 12.3/13, 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5, and Tax/IP is folded in.
- **Buyer wants:** Separate Title, Tax, IP, payment-obligation and covenant categories, each with its own limitation provisions and no general-regime override.
- **Recommendation: REJECT.** The "all Claims" drafting is a hidden override that would collapse every bespoke protection into the 20%/18-month package.

**SPA-N-015 Title verification**
- **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the DD-012 share register.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority, such as an ASIC search, encumbrance/PPSR search, constitution and share-issue records, and board/shareholder authority.
- **Recommendation: REJECT reliance on DD-012 alone.** It is an internal source the Seller supplied, and DL 10 concedes the Buyer has not verified it.

**SPA-N-016 Tax/IP open terms**
- **Seller:** Tax and IP are "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer wants:** Tax and IP treated as OPEN, with no deemed resolution. We should assume neither unlimited liability nor that the general regime applies.
- **Recommendation: REJECT the "settled" characterisation.** These terms remain open under our playbook and should be negotiated separately.

---

## Suggested next steps
- Respond in writing that the Buyer does not accept the "[STANDARD]/FINAL" categorisation and that all clauses remain open.
- Confirm with Amelia Frost that she has given no authority for the 20% cap, the 18-month period or a post-Completion Riverlark release. If the Seller insists she has, request written evidence.
- Send information requests on Bluefen cl. 11.3 conditions, the Riverlark payout figure, bonus on-costs, Ironquay payment evidence, DD-006 investigation status, Sandbar contract terms and title searches.
- Separately, check that the lease (DD-007) notification and the Mossvale (DD-009) assignment restriction are captured as completion deliverables or covenants. Neither appears to require consent, but both should be tracked.
